scope.summary: Implement the license guard tripwire per Section 13.16 (BK-16.5 license law) and the 05-daz license findings: fail-closed rejection of SMPL/SMPL-X/STAR, .dhdm, and Genesis-derived payloads at every morph/mesh import boundary using magic-byte, URI/filename, and metadata heuristics PLUS a mandatory closed-vocabulary license_tag on every morph asset (no tag = rejected). SMPL's license prohibits pornographic use (verified), so this guard protects the product's core legality; the only whitelisted external lineage is the one-time MakeHuman CC0 bootstrap.
acceptance_criteria: check_payload_license(bytes, declared_tag, source_uri) rejects: .dhdm magic/extension, SMPL/SMPL-X/STAR indicators (known npz/pickle layout markers, 'smpl' tokens in metadata/URI), and Daz DSON/Genesis payloads carrying Daz asset ids — each with a distinct typed rejection reason.
Rejection is fail-closed: any heuristic hit, missing license_tag, or unknown tag blocks the write BEFORE guard_authority_write; nothing lands in bodykit_morph_assets or base-mesh storage.
license_tag vocabulary is a closed enum: 'original' and 'makehuman_cc0_bootstrap' pass; free-text tags are rejected.
Every rejection emits a tailor.body ledger event with the rejection reason and a source fingerprint so attempted imports are auditable.
Tests cover a fake .dhdm payload, an SMPL-marker payload, a Daz DSON morph payload, a missing-tag asset (all rejected) and a clean 'original' asset (accepted).
scope.risk_if_missed: A single SMPL- or Genesis-derived asset entering authority contaminates the product line legally — SMPL explicitly bars pornographic use and Daz's EULA bars mesh/topology reuse — and no downstream validation can launder it out; fail-closed at the import boundary is the only safe posture.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit projects and base assets

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
